newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar opens stronger on overnight buying.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar opens stronger on overnight buying.

text.p: * The Canada dollar opened stronger in light trading at C$1.3835 (US$0.7228) as investors continued to bet against the possibility of a U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike on May 20, traders said. * They said they expected the dollar rally to resume as long as U.S. payrolls numbers due this morning do not surpass expectations.
But other analysts warned that the recent rally could set up the currency for a disastrous turn if signs of U.S. inflation return to haunt the market.
"It's a very dangerous bet," said another trader. "The Canadian dollar is undervalued and moving in the right direction, but the timing is stupid."
The surge in the Canada dollar was also helped by some substantial overnight selling of the British pound.
The pound traded weaker following the British Labour Party's overwhelming victory in yesterday's general election and amid speculation of a future devaluation of the currency.
The London Times suggested that a devaluation would be necessary to implement Labour's platform during the next five years.
The Canadian dollar has also benefitted from a surge in the bond market during the past three trading sessions.

"The rally in the bond market and the currency have been mutually reinforcing, and it's all based on optimism that the Fed doesn't need to raise rates on May 20," said Rob Palombi, senior fixed income analyst with MMS International.
Traders said the lack of political volatility in the Canadian election campaign was also underpinning the dollar.
Early polls show the Liberal government holding a commanding lead over the opposition parties.
"Nothing scary has really come out of the election so far," Palombi said. "If anything, the apparent slide in Bloc (Quebecois) support has reassured the markets."
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.2452 marks from Thursday's close of 1.2413 and jumped to 91.61 yen from Thursday's 91.15 yen.
